title: AtomicInteger — lock-free thread safety via CAS (Compare-And-Swap), when to use

s1_definition.profdef: `AtomicInteger` provides thread-safe integer operations WITHOUT locks — using hardware **CAS** (Compare-And-Swap). CAS is a single CPU instruction (`CMPXCHG` on x86) that atomically: reads the current value, compares it to an expected value, and if they match, writes the new value. If they don't match (another thread changed it), CAS fails and the operation retries in a loop. This is **lock-free** — no thread is ever BLOCKED. No monitor, no deadlock risk, no context switching. Methods: `get()`, `set()`, `incrementAndGet()`, `decrementAndGet()`, `addAndGet(delta)`, `compareAndSet(expected, update)`, `getAndUpdate(function)`, `updateAndGet(function)`. Use for: counters, sequence generators, accumulators, flags, and any single-variable atomic operation.
s1_definition.analogy: A MECHANICAL TOKEN DISPENSER at the bank counter. You press the button → the number advances by 1 → you get your token. Even if 10 people press simultaneously, the mechanism PHYSICALLY ensures each press advances by 1 — no two people get the same number. No lock on the machine. No waiting in line to press. The machine handles collisions internally (CAS retry). If two people press at the EXACT same instant, the hardware resolves it — one gets the number, the other's press retries and gets the next number.
s1_definition.oneliner: AtomicInteger = lock-free, CAS-based, single CPU instruction. incrementAndGet() = atomic read+increment+write. No locks, no blocking, no deadlock. Use for counters and single-variable updates.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `AtomicInteger` provides thread-safe integer operations WITHOUT locks — using hardware **CAS** (Compare-And-Swap). CAS is a single CPU instruction (`CMPXCHG` on x86) that atomically: reads the current value, compares it to an expected value, and if they match, writes the new value. If they don't match (another thread changed it), CAS fails and the operation retries in a loop. This is **lock-free** — no thread is ever BLOCKED. No monitor, no deadlock risk, no context switching. Methods: `get()`, `set()`, `incrementAndGet()`, `decrementAndGet()`, `addAndGet(delta)`, `compareAndSet(expected, update)`, `getAndUpdate(function)`, `updateAndGet(function)`. Use for: counters, sequence generators, accumulators, flags, and any single-variable atomic operation.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A MECHANICAL TOKEN DISPENSER at the bank counter. You press the button → the number advances by 1 → you get your token. Even if 10 people press simultaneously, the mechanism PHYSICALLY ensures each press advances by 1 — no two people get the same number. No lock on the machine. No waiting in line to press. The machine handles collisions internally (CAS retry). If two people press at the EXACT same instant, the hardware resolves it — one gets the number, the other's press retries and gets the next number.

**One line to remember:** AtomicInteger = lock-free, CAS-based, single CPU instruction. incrementAndGet() = atomic read+increment+write. No locks, no blocking, no deadlock. Use for counters and single-variable updates.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The trade execution service needed three atomic operations:** (1) Trade sequence number — each trade gets a unique incrementing ID. 200 threads generating IDs simultaneously. (2) Active order count — incremented on new order, decremented on fill/cancel. Dashboard displays real-time count. (3) Daily volume accumulator — each trade adds its quantity to a running total. All needed to be thread-safe, high-performance, no locks. Solution: `AtomicInteger` for sequence and active orders, `AtomicLong` for volume accumulator.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** 100 threads each call `sequence.incrementAndGet()` 1000 times. CAS internally: Thread-1 reads 499, computes 500, CAS(499→500) succeeds. Thread-2 reads 499 simultaneously, computes 500, CAS(499→500) FAILS (now 500) → retries: reads 500, computes 501, CAS(500→501) succeeds.

**Step 2.** After all threads: sequence = exactly 100,000. All 100,000 IDs are unique — no duplicates, no gaps.

**Step 3.** Active orders: 50 threads increment (new order), sleep 10ms, decrement (filled). At peak: up to 50 active. After all: exactly 0.

**Step 4.** updateAndGet for max price: each thread atomically compares its price with current max and updates if larger. CAS ensures no lost updates.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ CAS (Compare-And-Swap) — how it works ═══

  Thread-1:                          Thread-2:
  read(499)                          read(499)
  compute(500)                       compute(500)
  CAS(499→500) (Recommended) success!          CAS(499→500) fail! (now 500)
                                     retry: read(500)
                                     compute(501)
                                     CAS(500→501) (Recommended) success!

  Result: 501. Both increments counted! No lock!

  ═══ AtomicInteger METHODS ═══
  get()               → volatile read
  set(n)              → volatile write
  incrementAndGet()   → CAS loop: read→+1→CAS→retry
  compareAndSet(e,u)  → single CAS: if current==e, set u
  updateAndGet(fn)    → CAS loop: read→fn(v)→CAS→retry
  addAndGet(delta)    → CAS loop: read→+delta→CAS→retry
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — AtomicInteger Internals ═══

  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  AtomicInteger (java.util.concurrent.atomic)│
  │  ──────────────────────────────────────── │
  │  - value: volatile int                    │
  │  - VALUE: VarHandle (memory access)       │
  │  ──────────────────────────────────────── │
  │  + get(): int                             │ volatile read
  │  + set(int): void                         │ volatile write
  │  + incrementAndGet(): int                 │
  │    do {                                    │
  │      old = get();                          │
  │      next = old + 1;                       │
  │    } while (!CAS(old, next));             │ hardware CMPXCHG
  │    return next;                            │
  │  + compareAndSet(exp, upd): boolean       │ single CAS
  │  + updateAndGet(IntUnaryOperator): int    │ CAS + custom fn
  │  + accumulateAndGet(x, IntBinaryOp): int  │ CAS + binary fn
  └───────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Hardware CAS instruction (x86):
  LOCK CMPXCHG [addr], expected, newValue
  → if memory[addr] == expected: memory[addr] = newValue, return true
  → else: return false (another thread changed it)
  → ONE atomic CPU instruction! Uninterruptible!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
AtomicInteger provides lock-free thread safety using hardware CAS (Compare-And-Swap). `incrementAndGet()` internally loops: reads the current value, computes the new value, then CAS writes — if another thread changed the value, CAS fails and the loop retries with the fresh value. This is a single CPU instruction (CMPXCHG on x86) — no monitor lock, no blocking, no deadlock, no context switching. Excellent for counters, sequence generators, and single-variable atomic operations.

Key methods: `incrementAndGet()`/`decrementAndGet()` for counters, `compareAndSet(expected, update)` for state transitions (PENDING→ACTIVE), `updateAndGet(function)` for atomic custom logic (tracking maximum price), `addAndGet(delta)` for accumulators. Under high contention (100+ threads all CAS-ing the same variable), CAS retries increase — use `LongAdder` instead (striped cells, each thread increments its own cell). In banking: trade sequence generator → `AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet()` generates unique IDs for 200 concurrent threads. Active order count → increment on new order, decrement on fill. Daily volume → `AtomicLong.addAndGet(quantity)`.

---

keyPoints: CAS: read current, compute new, swap if unchanged
If changed by another thread, retry (spin)
